title: Cash-flow model for a home-services marketplace
scenario:
TOPIC: Evaluate cash flow and unit economics for a home-services marketplace
A marketplace plans to charge customers ₹2,000 per job, keep a 20% take rate, pay technicians every Friday, and refund customers within 48 hours when jobs fail. The launch plan assumes 300 jobs in month one, 8% refunds, ₹500 acquisition cost per completed job, ₹90,000 fixed monthly costs, and a ₹4 lakh opening balance. Rank the financial objections, calculate what happens in a conservative case with half the volume and double the refund rate, identify missing inputs, address cash timing, design a cheap validation test, and give an explicit funding verdict with conditions.

bad_signs.name: ignores settlement timing
bad_signs.pattern: cash flow is not a concern|timing does not matter

improvement_suggestions: Separate gross transaction value from what the company actually retains.
Model the order in which receipts, provider payments, and customer reversals occur.
Test the fragile assumption through a small manual cohort before scaling.
